analyst_view.overall: Fifth-placed Como (26 points, WWWLW) host sixth-placed Juventus (21 points) on Sunday evening in a top-six game; the numbers lean slightly to Como, who have scored 16 in their last six. Both sides play midweek: Como faced AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday and Juventus hosted Omonia in the Europa League on Thursday, where Spalletti was expected to rotate, so his first choices should be fresher here. Cesc Fabregas is without Kean, Jesus Rodriguez and Addai (the numbers count Kean and Diao), while Chalobah is back according to one report; Juventus miss Yildiz, Thuram, Locatelli and Grabara, and Kalulu and Nico Gonzalez may return (sources disagree). Referee Maurizio Mariani (3.9 cards a game) is already counted; news for this match was thin, with no dedicated Italian preview found, so the view stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals, 1.2 for Como, already taking off Diao and Kean and counting Como's 16 goals in six. Kean and Rodriguez have been out since October, so Como's form was built without them, and Juventus have been without Yildiz, Thuram and Locatelli for weeks; with no new absences found, I stay at about 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, 4.3 for Juventus, already nudged up for Juve's 44 corners in six. Como's possession game through Nico Paz, Da Cunha and Baturina is unchanged by the injuries up front, and Juve's wide play with Conceicao (who may make the squad) and Cambiaso continues, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already cut sharply because Como have been booked only 3 times in six (-19%) and Juve 8, and nudged up for referee Maurizio Mariani (3.9 a game). A top-six clash could be tighter than Como's quiet run suggests, but there is no rivalry edge and no suspension news, so I stay at about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots, 15.4 for Como, already raised for Como's shooting against a Juve side that has allowed 91 in six. Both teams played midweek, Como one day earlier than Juve, and Juve were expected to rest players against Omonia, so the fatigue roughly cancels out; I stay at about 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target, already lowered for Juventus's recent accuracy (-6.6%). Como again rely on Douvikas up front, as against AEK, and Juventus are still without Yildiz, so nothing new points either way; I stay at about 7.8.
